skill_entry.name: 6. Claim wider than the code: guarantees, timed paths, element counts and defaults
skill_entry.trigger: Four sentence kinds in body, commit message, Note, README, doc/ or file header; expand plurals, 'and', 'or', 'both', 'either', 'every' to one subject per row. (a) Type guarantee: a rejected input ('bare pointer') plus a compile-time mechanism word. (b) Measured path: an added timer or counter in h/ or src/ (rdtsc, inc_relaxed, fetch_add, *_cycles, note_*) whose sentence has a whole-word path word ('ends when', 'whichever', 'in both', 'either', 'every'; 'or the', 'and the' only beside the identifier). (c) Element count: an added production [0] or .front() read of a growable container, or a bare !empty() assert, plus a doc, Note or header cardinality sentence. (d) Stated default: the diff changes a default or its sentence; another literal states it.
skill_entry.procedure: 1. One row per subject: property, path or mechanism, text location. 2. (a): resolve each parameter type through every `using`; grade levels 1-3 (explicit constructor; no pointer constructor; distinct class) with the deciding line; read tests for opposite probes. 3. (b): map identifier to label; list every start, stop and increment site at HEAD; per named path find its selector and wait, the enclosing function of each stamp and the branch guarding its call; write start, stop or 'untimed'; tie a 0 in the review-time sample to the untimed path via the sibling counter. 4. (c): growers and call sites versus the cardinality sentence. 5. (d): every literal bound to the setting; the compile_definitions line. 6. One finding per subject.
skill_entry.question: For every subject the sentence covers (each type, each path, each element count, each build path), which line of the code reaches what the sentence says, and does the sentence say where it stops?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A limitation named in the sentence's own row or comment block, or in the body ('inert until #N wires it in'); 'typed' alone; `explicit` as such. A `#define S 0` fallback when CMake defines S only on the ON path (PR 3093): ask, accept the answer. Text narrowed instead of code widened closes a (b) finding. A plural handled by a loop; one accumulator bracketing every named part. .back(), a stack top, a fixed array index, a string receiver, test files. A cap on a setting; a re-spelled getenv, fallback unchanged. Owned elsewhere: CI-subject default (7); duplicate constant (13); [0] on a multi-device set (index-count); env var without comment; wrong identifier in the body (stale-body); misnamed flag (comment-contradicts, 5106398334).
skill_entry.finding_shape: (a): "`<alias>` (<file:line>) is an alias of the generic `<template>`, and <test:line> asserts it is constructible from `<pointer type>`. So any wrapped pointer or same-shaped view passes `<kernel>`; '<claim>' holds for <distinct-type subjects> only. Please say so in the description." (b), (c): "`<identifier>` is only <timed | read> at <file:line>, on the <path>. The <other path> at <file:line> is <never timed | reads `chunks[0]`>. So <`<metric>` reads 0 on <configuration>; the sample's 0 comes from that config | spec and function disagree>; '<claim>' holds for <subject> only. Either <time the poll | assert size() == 1>, or narrow the text." (d), a question: "would it make sense to flip <literal> to <value> at the same time, to make things consistent?"
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: Normal, as a statement, for a timer or guarantee claim: a fact, 'So <consequence>', then two remedies ('Either time the SW poll too ..., or narrow the docs'); the timer finding (4125033634) was the first of the five inline comments of his PR 4596 review 5342222359 (lowest id; review body: 'A few correctness and semantics issues inline, plus two design questions') and carried no severity word. 'Fine as a first step, but please say so in the description' for a staged type guarantee. A question for a spec-versus-code gap ('So is the spec wrong? Or are these functions insufficient?'). Minor, question form, for a default literal ('would it make sense to flip this to 1 at the same time, to make things consistent?'), approved regardless of the answer. Never blocking, never CHANGES_REQUESTED.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk; full file at HEAD (the timer's other paths and the enclosing function of each stamp, the unchanged `#ifndef` lines 40 lines below the hunk); other files (README*.md, doc/*.md, CMakeLists.txt, the Note's header, view.hpp for aliases); PR body at review time (GraphQL userContentEdits) including its sample output; callers (the functions that grow a container and their call sites; the increment site of the sibling path counter); the tests' constructibility probes. Not CI, not runtime.

final.procedure_commands:
## Check 6: claim wider than the code (guarantees, timed paths, element counts, defaults)

Setup for a merged PR (applies to every kind): HEAD = the commit the review names (the `### inline <id> at <time>` header of the digest, or the review's commit field). `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` returns HEAD itself for a merged PR and gives an empty diff, so take BASE = `git -C WT merge-base HEAD M^1` where M = `git -C WT log --merges --first-parent --format=%H --grep='#N' origin/main | head -1`. On PR 4596: M = c1331f3fb2, M^1 = 9b60b69dce, BASE = 66c7bb8db1 (diff 1891 lines, 10 files).

Step 1 (kind (a)), replace the grep with a prose-only one: `grep -n -i -E 'compile error|cannot be (passed|handed)|reject|enforce|no (bare|raw|public) pointer|STATIC_REQUIRE|static_assert|typed view so that|neither takes' body.md log.txt; grep -n -E '^\+\s*(//|\*)' pr.diff | grep -i -E '<same pattern>'; git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- doc 'README*.md' | grep -n -i -E '<same pattern>'`. A `static_assert` code line and a register JSON `desc` string ('enforced at the bottom of each Systolic Column', PRs 2180/3631) are the enforcing declaration or hardware prose, not a claim. Steps 2-7 stay as written.

Append after the existing "On PR 4557" line:

8. Measured-path claims. Timers and counters the diff adds, code only: `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- h src t | grep -n -E '^\+.*(rdtsc\(\)|inc_relaxed\(|fetch_add\(|_cycles\b|note_[a-z_]+\()'`; a doc/*.md or script line is never an added timer (PR 2203 doc line 'usage_time = rdtsc()'). Map each identifier X to its label L first: `grep -n -o -E 'T[0-9] = .*' body.md` and `git -C WT show HEAD:h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp | grep -n -o -E 'T[0-9] = [^.]*'` (gives `T5 = join_wait_cycles`). Then per X: `grep -n -E "X|\bL\b" body.md`; and sentence-level over the repository, because a doc sentence wraps and a Note names a timer by its label: `for f in README.stats.md h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp <files of the diff>; do git -C WT show HEAD:$f | tr '\n' ' ' | grep -o -E "[^.]*(X|\bL\b)[^.]*\."; done`. Keep the sentences that match the whole-word filter `grep -w -i -E 'ends when|whichever|in both|either|every'`; keep 'or the' and 'and the' only when the same sentence names X or L. (`-w` keeps 'neither' out: PR 2693 comment '0 = neither K nor V saved' matched the old filter through the substring 'either' and matches `-w` 0 times; README.stats.md:261 still matches through 'ends when'.) One subject row per path named. Clear a sentence whose X is one accumulator with one start and one stop that bracket every named part (`X -= rdtsc()` before the first part, `X += ...` after the last, no `return` or `continue` between): body.md:19 (T2 'both passes and the join', attn_elapsed :820 to :852 around run_joins :843) clears this way.
9. For each named path find the selector and the wait in the file at HEAD: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | grep -n -E 'const bool (join_hw|uses_hw)|if \((!)?(join_hw|uses_hw)|hw_plan\.empty|continue;  // poll|while \(!'` (drop parameter and signature lines; the plain `uses_hw|stats_enabled` grep gives 40 hits in a 2078-line file, 30 of them signatures). Then the stamps of X: `git -C WT show HEAD:<file> | grep -n -E 'X|t_wait|t_poll|rdtsc'`. For each start or stop stamp name its enclosing function (`awk 'NR<=<stamp line> && /^    [a-z_:<>]+ [a-z_]+\(/ {l=NR": "$0} END{print l}'`) and the line that calls that function; the branch guarding the call (`if (join_hw)` for stream_hw_joins) is the path the stamp belongs to. Write per path: start line, stop line, or "untimed" (no stamp between the selector and the `note_*` call).
10. Sample output at review time: `gh api graphql -f query='query{repository(owner:"positron-ai",name:"tron"){pullRequest(number:N){userContentEdits(first:30){nodes{editedAt diff}}}}}'`; take the review timestamp from the digest and read the `diff` field of the latest edit before it (the field holds the full body, not a unified diff). Then `grep -n -E '"X":0' body.md README*.md`. For each hit read the whole sample block and the prose line that introduces it; the configuration comes from a path counter in the same block (`fpga_k_tokens`, `fpga_queries`: `git -C WT grep -n 'note_fpga_pass(' HEAD -- h src` gives its increment site and the branch it sits in; 0 there means that path never ran, so the selector of that path was false), `n_workers` in the summary block, and the run shape in the prose. A 0 for X with the other path's counter also 0 is the consequence sentence. A zero is a finding candidate, never evidence of no work.
11. Element-count claims, production files only: `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -n -E '^\+.*(\[0\]|\.front\(\))'`. Drop a hit whose receiver is a string (`std::string`, `string_view`, `const char*`: attn_stats.hpp `id.front() == '.'`), whose container has no grower in h/ or src/ (fixed array `bf16* x[N]`, `std::array`, `listeners[2]`), or whose removed twin differs only by whitespace (PR 2135 `attn[0].finish`). `.back()` reads, a stack top and an append-or-extend branch (PR 4353 `worker_plan.back()` after push_back, PR 2545 `shard_stack.back()`) do not trigger. For each container C use the full member expression (`pool.chunks`, never a bare word under 6 characters): `git -C WT grep -n -i -E 'one or more|multiple|several|a list of|exactly one|at most one' HEAD -- doc 'README*.md' h src | grep -i 'C'`; growers: `git -C WT grep -n -E 'C\.(push_back|emplace_back|insert|resize)\(' HEAD -- h src`; call sites of the growing function F: `git -C WT grep -n -E '\bF\(' HEAD -- h src t`. The cardinality sentence must name C itself, not its element type.
12. Default claims. Setting name S from the hunk: `grep -n -E 'option\(|default (ON|OFF)|getenv' pr.diff`; a re-spelled getenv line whose fallback value is unchanged (PR 2475 `TRON_POISON_BITS`) does not change a default. Every literal bound to S: `git -C WT grep -n -E "S" HEAD -- CMakeLists.txt 'src/*/CMakeLists.txt' h src doc 'README*.md'`; the define line: `git -C WT grep -n -E "compile_definitions\(.*S" HEAD`. When the define sits inside `if(S)`, a `#ifndef S / #define S 0` is the OFF path (deliberate, ask only); when nothing defines S, the fallback is the real default and must match the stated one. A cap on the same setting (`std::min(parsed, max_...)`, PR 4353 `16` beside the fallback `8`) is not a second statement of the default. A getenv whose every bound literal carries the same value stops here with one line 'S: N literals, all <value>' (PR 4596 `TRON_ATTN_STATS`: 7 lines, all 'exactly 1').
13. Truth table and findings as in steps 6-7: one finding per failing subject, anchored at the code line (the alias definition, the timer start, the [0] read, the fallback literal); the body row, README line and test comment are citations.

On PR 4596 (review 5342222359 at 1430736b2a; BASE 66c7bb8db1): step 8 finds `join_wait_cycles` (h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp:1027 parameter, :1188 accumulator), label T5; the body at review (edit of 2026-09-25T22:31:45Z, line 22) and the sentence-level grep on README.stats.md:260-262 and h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:37-39 name two paths ("an FPGA pass or the other workers' software partials"). Step 9: selector `join_hw` at :1251; hardware path start :1132 (`t_wait = ... rdtsc()`), stop :1147, both inside `stream_hw_joins` (:1020), called at :1304-1306 only under `if (join_hw)` at :1300; software path poll at :1258 `if (!join_hw && plan_state.sections_left[kv_head]) continue;  // poll` with no rdtsc between :1251 and :1315 = untimed; attn_stats.hpp:421 drops a zero. Step 10: body line 94 `"join_wait_cycles":0,"fpga_k_tokens":0`, note_fpga_pass called only at self_attention.hpp:636 inside the hardware pass builder, so `join_hw` was false on every layer = the untimed path. Finding = 4125033634; the author timed the poll in 6e2310174460 and the README now says "measured in both join modes".

On PR 3093 (review 4603858419 and approval 4603901812, both at 6590b12915): step 12 with S = TRON_ARENA_ALLOCATOR_DEFAULT_ON: src/system/memory.cpp:32 (the only changed line, comment "default ON"), :71-73 (`#ifndef ... / #define ... 0 / #endif`, unchanged), :80 (reader `!= 0`), src/system/CMakeLists.txt:65 (`option(... ON)`), :66-68 (`target_compile_definitions(system PRIVATE ...=1)` inside `if(...)`), doc/pos_heap_v2.md:777-778 ("default ON"); h/system/memory.hpp:24 names the macro without a value. The define exists only on the ON path, so the 0 is the OFF-path fallback: question only (3501641254), closed by the author's answer, approved 6 min 47 s later at the same commit.

On PR 2713 (review 4273601429 at 25d146aa1596; c239894b75 = e4c4f49452~1 is the head before the fix and src/system/memory.cpp is identical in both): step 11 finds `h->pool.chunks[0].base` at src/system/memory.cpp:198 and `.chunks[0].size` at :209, each after a `!h->pool.chunks.empty()` assert (:197, :208); doc/pos_heap_v2.md:401 says "mmap that budget as one or more chunks"; grower `pool.chunks.push_back` at src/system/heap_v2.cpp:287 inside `expand()` (:262) (the same lines sit at :296 and :324 in ff19045fd0); production call sites of `expand(`: src/system/memory.cpp:131 only; t/t_heap_v2.cpp calls `h.expand(` 20 times on 24 heaps, never twice on one heap; doc:449 "No runtime growth path in v1". Finding = 3227529208 as a question; the author replaced both asserts with `TRON_ASSERT_EQ(h->pool.chunks.size(), 1u)` in e4c4f49452 (the reply 3228805183 names it bc61dfa4c; both ids exist with the same subject), visible at ff19045fd0:src/system/memory.cpp:204 and :215 with the comment at :193-199.

On PR 4557 (review 5420005787 at 96a6220ab664, approval at c5d44bd86f): the existing "On PR 4557" line holds at 96a6220ab664 (K probe t/t_llama_unit.cpp:397); at c5d44bd86f the probe is :394 and the author added the comment block :388-391 ("does not enforce it") after the review.

SKILL.md, "The thirteen questions", replace item 6 with "6. Claim sentence: for every subject it covers (each type, each path, each element count, each build path), which code line reaches what the sentence says, and does the sentence say where it stops?"

SKILL.md, "Words used here", BASE line: append "For a merged PR, `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` returns HEAD; take BASE = `git merge-base HEAD M^1` where M is the merge commit of the PR on origin/main."

SKILL.md, check 6, replace the trigger paragraph that begins "Trigger, all parts: a sentence in the PR body, a commit message, a Note or a comment names a rejected input" and ends "Expand every plural or \"and\" into its subjects." with:
"Trigger, any one of four sentence kinds, in the PR body, a commit message, a Note, a README hunk, a file under doc/ or a file-header comment. Expand every plural, 'and', 'or', 'both', 'either' and 'every' into one subject per row. (a) Type guarantee: the sentence names a rejected input ('bare pointer', 'raw pointer', 'the other plane's view', 'cannot be passed', 'cannot be handed in') and gives a compile-time reason (a mechanism word: 'compile error', 'rejected', 'enforced', 'STATIC_REQUIRE', 'static_assert', or the parameter type as the reason: 'passed as its typed view so that', 'neither takes'); only prose triggers, never a static_assert code line or a register description string. (b) Measured path: the diff adds a timer or counter in h/ or src/ (rdtsc(), the cycle-counter read; inc_relaxed(; fetch_add(; a *_cycles field; a note_*( hook) and a sentence naming it, or its label (T5), carries a whole-word path word ('ends when', 'whichever', 'in both', 'either', 'every'; 'or the' and 'and the' only when the same sentence names the identifier or label). A counter whose callers the body defers to a named later PR ('inert until #N wires it in') is a staged limitation stated in the PR and does not fire. (c) Element count: an added production line reads [0] or .front() of a container that has a grow function (push_back, emplace_back, insert, resize) as if it were the whole, or asserts only !empty() before such a read, and a doc/*.md sentence, Note or header comment names that container next to a cardinality word ('one or more', 'multiple', 'several', 'a list of'). A .back() read, a stack top, an append-or-extend branch, an index into a fixed-size array and a string receiver do not trigger; the cardinality sentence must name the container, not its element type. (d) Stated default: the diff changes a default or a sentence stating one (a CMake option(ON|OFF), a '(default ON)' comment, a getenv fallback, a config literal) for a setting name whose value is stated a second time by another literal (a '#ifndef S / #define S <v>' fallback, a doc table row, a second constant with the same meaning). A cap or bound on the same setting (std::min(parsed, max_...)) is not a second statement of the default, and a re-spelled getenv line whose fallback is unchanged does not change a default."

SKILL.md, check 6, keep the procedure paragraph "Procedure: for each subject, find every parameter in the diff's added lines ..." through "... with the other locations as citations." and add after it:
"Kind (b): map the identifier to its label first, then list every start stamp, stop stamp and increment site of the identifier in the file at HEAD. For each path the sentence names, find the branch variable that selects it (`join_hw`, `uses_hw`, `!hw_plan.empty()`) and the wait on that path (a `continue;  // poll`, a `while (!ready)`, a spin). For each stamp name its enclosing function and the branch that guards the call of that function; that branch is the stamp's path. Write per path: start line, stop line, or 'untimed'. Clear a sentence whose identifier is one accumulator with one start and one stop that bracket every named part. Then read the sample output of the body as it stood at review time (GraphQL userContentEdits, the latest edit before the review): a 0 for the metric in a block whose sibling path counter (`fpga_k_tokens`) is also 0 shows the configuration of the untimed path and is the consequence sentence. A zero is a finding candidate, never evidence of no work.
Kind (c): grep doc/*.md, Notes and header comments for the container's full member expression next to a cardinality word; find every function that grows the container and count the call sites of that function in src/, h/ and t/. If the doc allows N elements and the code handles one, ask which is right and request an assert on size() == 1 or a doc fix.
Kind (d): grep every literal bound to the setting name in CMakeLists.txt files, h/, src/, doc/ and README*.md. When the build defines the macro only on the ON path, a `#ifndef S / #define S 0` fallback is the OFF path and is deliberate; when nothing defines it, the fallback is the real default and must agree with the stated one. A getenv whose every bound literal carries the same value stops at the grep.
The sentence holds only if every subject reaches the claimed property on the claimed path, or the text names the subjects or paths it does not cover. Anchor each finding at the code line (the alias definition, the timer start, the [0] read, the fallback literal); the body row, README line and test comment are citations."

SKILL.md, check 6, keep the sentence "Do not fire on: a sentence whose own table row or own comment block names the limitation; the word \"typed\" alone; an `explicit` constructor as such." and the two sentences after it; replace "once the text states it" with "once the PR body or the sentence's own comment block states it", and append:
"Also not: a second literal that is the fallback for the opposite build path when the CMake line defines the macro only on the ON path (PR 3093: the author answered that `#define ... 0` is the option-OFF fallback and Wade approved 7 minutes later at the same commit); ask it as a question and accept the answer when the CMake line shows it. A timer or counter whose text the author narrows instead of widening the code: both repairs close the finding, and no new instrumentation design is required once the narrower scope is written down. A plural the code handles by construction (a loop over the container or over the paths; one accumulator around every named part). A doc-only PR: kind (c) runs only when the PR adds or changes the code that reads the container. Owned by other checks: a default sentence with a CI subject is check 7; a second named constant with the same value is check 13; a [0] read with no doc cardinality sentence but a multi-device or multi-worker runtime set is the index-count-or-wait-set-mismatch check (3029339639); a new env-var read with no comment is the missing-explanation check (3036997452); a body sentence that names an identifier the code does not have (PR 2875 `pins_below` versus `subtree_pins`) is the stale-body check (8/9); a comment or label that misnames an identifier, a path or a flag on the line it sits on is the comment-contradicts check (the PR 3490 'Perfetto option' nit, 5106398334, has that shape)."
